fig1_phase_space_streaming.svg: Collisionless phase mixing from the module's free_stream: a density ripple $f=e^{-v^2/2}(1+\tfrac12\cos x)$ (left) is advected to $f(x-vt,v)$ at $t=2/\omega$ (right). Fast and slow velocities shear at different rates, winding the ripple into fine diagonal filaments — yet $f$ is merely transported along orbits (Liouville, $df/dt=0$): the velocity marginal $\int f\,dx$ is frozen to 2e-16 and the Vlasov residual $\partial_t f+v\partial_x f$ is 1e-04 of the streaming term.
fig2_plasma_coupling.svg: Plasma coupling parameter $\Lambda=n\lambda_D^3$ over the density–temperature plane, evaluated by the module's plasma_parameter / debye_length. $\Lambda$ counts particles in a Debye sphere: above the $\Lambda=1$ line (orange) the plasma is weakly coupled and collective, so screening is statistically meaningful and the mean-field Vlasov equation holds ($\nu_{ei}/\omega_p\sim\ln\Lambda/\Lambda\ll1$); below it is strongly coupled. The star marks the demo plasma ($n=10^{18}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $T=1$ eV, $\Lambda\approx411$). Since $\Lambda\propto T^{3/2}/\sqrt n$, hotter and thinner plasmas are more ideal.
